assumptions: Exchangeability: the calibration windows and the windows the bound is applied to are exchangeable. In-domain the split is at CLIP level (LOCO), so the honest exchangeable unit is the clip, not the window.
One labeller: every label comes from the same human, so label noise is not modelled and no inter-rater variance is included in any interval.
The calibration scores are inner-LOCO out-of-fold: no calibration window's own clip trained the model that scored it.

Intra-clip correlation BREAKS window-level exchangeability. The repo already measured this (docs/FACTS.md): nominal 2.7 % false-reject became 46 % on held-out clips, intra-clip correlation 0.58, effective n about 11. That measurement is the repo's, not re-measured in this stream.

OOD-160 is a different distribution (an IndEgo-trained head applied to Egocentric-10K). No target exchangeability holds there, so an IndEgo-selected lambda carries no guarantee on OOD-160 and the OOD rows are descriptive.

The CRC rule bounds the expected risk of the SELECTED rule under a monotone risk curve; it is a statement about the calibration draw, not a per-window certificate, and it is not a licence to skip the audit.
Risk and coverage are defined as in CONFIG: coverage is the share auto-decided, risk the error among the auto-decided windows.
bound_wording: conformal-style bound under exchangeability, assumptions listed
ci95_type: clip-level bootstrap (resample 7 IndEgo clips, 2000 draws, seed 0) on the 100 %-coverage balanced accuracy of P1

config.coverage_definition: share of windows decided automatically; the rest go to a human
config.crc_rule: (n/(n+1))*risk_hat(lambda) + 1/(n+1) <= alpha; primary pick = smallest lambda that passes (crc_published); a monotone-envelope pick and an uncorrected pick are reported alongside
config.risk_definition: misclassification rate among the AUTO-DECIDED windows (both a false accept and a false reject count)

label_source: human gold, ONE labeller (150 IndEgo windows: 100 good / 50 bad) | human labels, ONE labeller (160 Egocentric-10K windows: 138 good / 22 bad; 19 of 22 bad are NO_ACTIVE_WORK)
notes: Risk at coverage c is measured on the auto-decided windows only; the reviewed windows are not counted as errors.
Confidence for P2 uses each window's own fold threshold, so the confidence is comparable across folds.
The frontier bootstrap re-selects the top-c fraction inside every resample, so the interval covers the selection as well as the metric.

All three policies are FORCED-decision policies (accept iff score >= threshold); the shipped cascade instead accepts outside the band at p >= 0.75. The forced variant is used so that the 100 %-coverage numbers are comparable across policies and with AUTO.00.

band_plus_second_view.why: the cached EmbeddingGemma-2 window embeddings cover the 150 IndEgo windows only; the OOD-160 windows have no cached second-view embedding and this stream did not run a model to make one

youden_perfold.why: one class missing at this coverage

ood_caveat: OOD-160: n=160, n_bad=22, and 19 of the 22 bad windows are NO_ACTIVE_WORK (2 HANDS_NOT_VISIBLE, 1 SHAKY); 47 factories; ONE human labeller. Intervals are factory-grouped; the window bootstrap is shown only marked optimistic.
protocol: coverage sweep over a confidence ranking with clip-grouped (IndEgo) / factory-grouped (OOD-160) bootstrap that re-selects inside every resample; conformal-style lambda chosen on training folds only (per outer fold for IndEgo, IndEgo-150 for OOD)
